mainTopic: Giving a loan as a gift, and whether someone who gives away a palm tree, or sells a house, keeps back part of it for himself
overview: The גמרא first looks at a שכיב מרע who gives away a loan that someone owes him, and asks how this works when a בריא normally cannot do it. רב פפא answers that a שכיב מרע's gift works like an inheritance, and heirs inherit loans. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא answers that even a בריא can give a loan, through מעמד שלשתן, as רב הונא taught in the name of רב. Next the גמרא asks a new question: if someone gives a דקל to one person and its fruit to another, does he keep back the 'place of the fruit' for the second person? It also asks what happens if he keeps the fruit for himself. רבא in the name of רב נחמן rules that when a person keeps something for himself, he keeps it בעין יפה (generously), so he keeps the place of the fruit too. Finally, רבי אבא tells רב אשי that his tradition taught this idea on a different case. That case is a ruling of רבי שמעון בן לקיש about a man who sells a house but keeps the upper story for himself.

steps.title: A dying man gives away a loan owed to him
steps.stepSummary: A שכיב מרע who says 'give my loan to so-and-so' succeeds: the loan goes to that person.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a dying man says, 'Give the loan people owe me to so-and-so,' then that person gets the loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: a שכיב מרע can give away money that someone owes him, and the gift works. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan is not a physical object the giver is holding. It is a debt sitting with someone else. Even so, the rule is that the loan really passes to the person the שכיב מרע names.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is dangerously ill, on his deathbed
A loan, meaning money owed to someone

phrases.english: A person on his deathbed who said: 'Give my loan to so-and-so' –
phrases.notes: 'My loan' means money that others owe him, not money he owes.

phrases.english: his loan goes to so-and-so,

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁכִיב מְרַע שֶׁאָמַר תְּנוּ הַלְוָאָתִי לִפְלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the sugya from the previous daf about the gifts of a שכיב מרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שכיב מרע can give a loan owed to him as a gift, and the receiver acquires it.

steps.title: But a healthy person cannot do this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out the surprise: a בריא cannot give away a loan like this, so how can a שכיב מרע?
steps.simpleTranslation: And this works even though it does not work for a healthy person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty with the rule it just stated: a healthy person cannot give away a loan this way. So why is a שכיב מרע different?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan without a שטר is not something a healthy person can normally hand over to someone else. Usually a שכיב מרע's gift follows the same basic limits as a healthy person's gift, so this rule needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not exist / it does not apply

phrases.english: and this is so even though it does not apply to a healthy person!
phrases.notes: A healthy person can't just hand over a debt that someone else owes him.

steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a שכיב מרע can give away a loan owed to him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A healthy person cannot transfer a loan this way, so why should a שכיב מרע be able to?

steps.title: רב פפא: an heir inherits loans
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that a שכיב מרע's gift is treated like an inheritance, and an heir does inherit loans.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Because an heir inherits a loan.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. A שכיב מרע's gift works like an inheritance, and heirs inherit loans owed to the dead person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא agrees that a healthy person cannot give a loan this way. He explains that a שכיב מרע is different because his gift works like a ירושה, and a loan passes to an heir without any act of transfer.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Since an heir inherits it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the loan. The idea is that a dying man's gift works like passing things on to an heir.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר הוֹאִיל וְיוֹרֵשׁ יוֹרְשָׁהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a שכיב מרע differs from a healthy person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שכיב מרע's gift should follow the same limits as a healthy person's gift.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שכיב מרע's gift is like ירושה, and loans are inherited, so his gift of a loan works.

steps.title: רב אחא: even a healthy person can give a loan
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא says the question is wrong from the start. A healthy person can also give a loan, through מעמד שלשתן, as רב הונא taught in the name of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא said: A healthy person can also give away a loan, following what רב הונא said in the name of רב: If someone says, 'You are holding a מנה of mine; give it to so-and-so,' and all three people are present, the third person acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא gives a different answer. He says a healthy person can also give away a loan, and he brings proof from רב הונא's rule of מעמד שלשתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא accepted the question and explained why a שכיב מרע is different. רב אחא rejects the question itself: a loan can be given by a healthy person when the lender, the borrower and the receiver are all present together. If so, there is no surprise that a שכיב מרע can do it too.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of one hundred זוז
In the presence of all three: the lender, the borrower and the receiver

steps.whyThisMatters: מעמד שלשתן is a well-known way to transfer a debt in practical הלכה, without any formal act of acquisition.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, said:
A loan can be given by a healthy person,
and this follows what Rav Huna said in the name of Rav –
as Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
'You are holding a maneh of mine; give it to so-and-so';
phrases.notes: The lender is talking to the borrower here, who still owes him the money.

phrases.english: if all three of them are present – he acquires it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר הַלְוָאָה אִיתָא בְּבָרִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 2 that is different from רב פפא's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A healthy person cannot give away a loan.
steps.terutzMaskana: A healthy person can give away a loan through מעמד שלשתן, so the rule for a שכיב מרע is not surprising.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why a שכיב מרע can give a loan: רב פפא says his gift works like ירושה; רב אחא says even a בריא can do it through מעמד שלשתן.

steps.title: A tree to one person, its fruit to another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if someone gives a דקל to one person and its fruit to another, did he keep back the 'place of the fruit' for the second person?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: If someone gives a palm tree to one person and its fruit to another, what is the law? Did he keep back the place of the fruit, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about giving a tree and its fruit to two different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit that has not grown yet cannot be given as a gift by itself. If the giver kept back the 'place of the fruit', meaning a piece of the tree, then the second person owns something real and gets the fruit through it. The question is whether giving the fruit separately automatically means keeping back that place.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them, an open question
The place of the fruit, the part of the tree where fruit grows

steps.confusionAlert: 'Place of the fruit' is not the fruit itself. It is a piece of the tree that someone owns, and through it he can get fruit that has not grown yet.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
A palm tree to one person and its fruit to another, what is the law?
Did he keep back the place of the fruit,
or did he not keep it back?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ דֶּקֶל לְאֶחָד וּפֵירוֹתָיו לְאַחֵר מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the loan discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether giving the fruit to a second person automatically means keeping back the place of the fruit for him.

steps.title: What if he keeps the fruit for himself?
steps.stepSummary: Even if giving the fruit to someone else does not count as keeping back its place, what if the giver keeps the fruit for himself?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that when the fruit goes to another person it is not counted as keeping back the place, then what if he says the tree is given 'except for its fruit', keeping the fruit for himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a follow-up question. Even if the first case does not count as keeping back the place, maybe keeping the fruit for oneself is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case changes from fruit going to a second person to fruit staying with the giver. The question is whether a person keeping something for himself is judged differently from a person giving it to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say, meaning: even if we answer the first question this way

phrases.english: If you will say:
for another person it is not a reservation;
for himself – 'except for its fruit', what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר לְאַחֵר לָא הָוֵי שִׁיּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the question of step 5 with a second case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether keeping the fruit for oneself counts as keeping back the place of the fruit.

steps.title: רב נחמן: for himself, he does keep the place
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רב נחמן rules that even if giving the fruit to another is not a reservation, keeping the fruit for oneself is a reservation of the place of the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: Even if you say that a tree to one person and its fruit to another does not keep back the place of the fruit, if he gave the tree to one person and kept its fruit for himself, he did keep back the place of the fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא, quoting רב נחמן, answers the second question: when the giver keeps the fruit for himself, he keeps the place of the fruit too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not decide the first question. He only says that even if the answer there is 'no', the case of keeping the fruit for oneself is 'yes'. So the two cases are treated differently.

phrases.english: Rava said in the name of Rav Naḥman:
Even if you will say:
a palm tree to one person and its fruit to another
is not a reservation of the place of the fruit;
a palm tree to one person, and he kept its fruit for himself –
he kept back the place of the fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the follow-up question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Keeping the fruit for oneself counts as keeping back the place of the fruit, even if giving the fruit to another does not.

steps.title: The reason: a person keeps things for himself generously
steps.stepSummary: The reason for the difference is that when a person keeps something for himself, he keeps it בעין יפה, generously.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Whatever a person keeps for himself, he keeps generously.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why keeping the fruit for oneself is different: people are generous with themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person keeps something for himself, we assume he means to keep as much as possible, so he keeps the place of the fruit too, not just the fruit. When he gives to someone else, we do not assume he gave more than he said.

keyTerms.meaning: With a good eye, meaning generously

steps.whatToRemember: A person who keeps something back for himself keeps it בעין יפה, so he keeps the place of the fruit and not just the fruit.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Anything with regard to himself –
he keeps back generously.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כֹּל לְגַבֵּי נַפְשֵׁיהּ בְּעַיִן יָפָה מְשַׁיֵּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the ruling in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person keeps things for himself generously, so he keeps the place of the fruit as well.

steps.title: רבי אבא says the teaching was learned on a different case
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא tells רב אשי that in his tradition, the idea that a person keeps things for himself בעין יפה was taught on a statement of רבי שמעון בן לקיש, not on the case of the דקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to רב אשי: We learned this teaching as connected to what רבי שמעון בן לקיש said.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא offers a different version of where the teaching from step 8 belongs. This line sets up the next move, which quotes the statement he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the idea of keeping something for yourself בעין יפה was attached to the case of the דקל and its fruit. רבי אבא says his tradition attached it to a different ruling, from רבי שמעון בן לקיש. The content of that ruling comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned it, meaning our tradition teaches it this way
On, or in connection with (short for על ד־)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבא is not arguing with the idea of בעין יפה. He only disagrees about which case it was originally taught on.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַן אַדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ.
phrases.english: We learned it on the statement of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish.
phrases.notes: "It" is the idea from just before: a person keeps something for himself generously.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנַן אַדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different tradition about where the בעין יפה principle from step 8 was taught
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי אבא's tradition, the בעין יפה principle was taught on a statement of רבי שמעון בן לקיש, not on the case of the דקל

steps.title: Selling a house but keeping the upper story
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש rules that if someone sells a house on condition that the upper story stays his, the upper story belongs to the seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: If someone sells a house to another person and tells him, 'on condition that the upper story is mine,' then the upper story is his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ruling of רבי שמעון בן לקיש that רבי אבא was talking about. A seller who holds back the upper floor keeps it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the seller keeps something for himself, just as in step 6 the giver kept the fruit for himself. The plain ruling, that the upper story stays with the seller, sounds obvious. This hints that the point of the case is connected to keeping things for oneself בעין יפה, which רבי אבא said was taught on this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper story or floor of a building

steps.whyThisMatters: In רבי אבא's version, this sale case, not the case of the דקל, is where רב נחמן's principle of keeping things for oneself בעין יפה was taught.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
One who sells a house to his fellow,
and said to him:
"On condition that the upper story is mine"
the upper story is his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the statement of רבי שמעון בן לקיש that רבי אבא mentioned in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If someone sells a house on condition that the upper story is his, the upper story remains the seller's
